title: Entity sample provenance notebook
content:
Purpose:
This is a personal scratchpad for tracking how we capture and use 'sample provenance' metadata for labelled entity spans. Goal is to reduce label noise, make deduping auditable, and enable stratified sampling for quality checks and model audits.

Background / motivation:
- We get lots of near-duplicate examples that look different but share the same source (scraped pages, same user across sessions, mirrored API responses). That inflates training/validation scores and makes drift detection noisier.
- Current labeling flow records only: doc_id, annotator_id, label, span_text. Missing: ingest_source, scrape_batch_id, original_url_hash, sampling_bucket, transform_pipeline.
- Need lightweight provenance fields that are easy for labelers to add and/or auto-fill during ingestion.

Minimum provenance schema (lightweight, human-readable):
- ingest_source: (string) e.g., sitemap, internal-api, user-upload, scrape-2025-07-04
- source_id: (string) identifier in upstream system (may be blank)
- source_fingerprint: (string) short hash of full source content (not the span) e.g., fh:7c9a
- pipeline_tag: (string) indicates transformations applied e.g., normalise-whitespace|de-id-pii
- sample_bucket: (string) used for stratified sampling, options: random, high-traffic-user, newly-sampled, adversarial-expansion
- derived_from: (string) record id of prior sample this was derived from (if copy/augmentation)
- evidence_url: (string) optional link to saved context snapshot or S3 object
- labeler_notes: (string) freeform quick note for edgecases

Design constraints:
- Keep fields short; prefer codes over long text where possible.
- Fields should be automatically computed on ingest when feasible (e.g., source_fingerprint, pipeline_tag).
- Labelers can edit or add labeler_notes and sample_bucket only. Avoid burdening labelers with many manual fields.

Heuristics for deduplication (operational):
1) Exact source_fingerprint match => candidate duplicate cluster.
2) If source_fingerprint differs but source_id (upstream identifier) matches => same origin, keep one per origin for training unless label differs.
3) Near-dup of span_text (Levenshtein <= 3 and same pipeline_tag) => mark as probable duplicate for reviewer.
4) If derived_from is populated, treat as a derived augmentation and downweight in train/val selection.

Sampling rules for QA checks:
- Frequency: weekly stratified sample of 500 items across buckets: random (250), high-traffic-user (100), newly-sampled (100), adversarial-expansion (50).
- De-duplication before sampling: collapse clusters by source_fingerprint and sample at most 2 per cluster.
- Keep audit history: save the provenance snapshot used for that week's sample in S3 and reference in Jira ticket for audit.

Labeler micro-guidelines for annotating provenance: (short, for UI sticky note)
- If you see the same text multiple times from different URLs, prefer to tag sample_bucket=high-traffic-user only if the user id/username is explicit in context.
- If original content looks autogenerated (templated), set pipeline_tag=templated and add labeler_notes explaining why.
- If you copy context into notes for context, mark evidence_url with the snapshot id.

Quick examples (literal lines to paste into tooltips):
- ingest_source: scrape-2025-10-07
- source_id: page://news/23345
- source_fingerprint: fh:3b9f
- pipeline_tag: normalise-whitespace|de-id
- sample_bucket: random
- derived_from: (blank)
- evidence_url: s3://redwood-qa/provenance/2025-10-07/23345.json

Edge cases and unresolved questions (notes-to-self):
- What to do with mirrored content across language variants? fingerprint of full-page + lang tag?
- Should we compute an "author fingerprint" (hash of author name + mailing id) to detect reposts? privacy risk—avoid storing real PII, maybe salt+hash with KMS.
- Downweight vs drop: for dedup clusters where labels disagree, we should keep top-k with label diversity and flag for adjudication rather than blind dedup.
- How to surface provenance fields in small-labeler UIs without clutter? Idea: collapsible "source details" panel with autofill and a 1-line editable sample_bucket + notes.

Snippet: provenance-quality-check script idea (pseudocode)
- cluster_by_fingerprint(samples)
- for cluster in clusters:
    if cluster.size > 6: mark cluster for heavy-prune
    keep = select_up_to_two_with_max_label_agreement(cluster)
    if label_conflict_detected(cluster): create_review_ticket(cluster.sample_ids)

Label auditing checklist (for weekly QA):
- Are there clusters where label disagreement > 30%? flag for adjudication.
- Are any pipeline_tags missing or suspicious (e.g., blank when expected)?
- Do snapshot evidence_urls resolve and contain full context?

Operational notes (implementation/ops):
- Low-effort path: add source_fingerprint and pipeline_tag to ingest; let labeltool show sample_bucket and labeler_notes.
- Medium-effort: integrate fingerprint dedupe in sampling service to avoid showing too many near-duplicates to labelers.
- High-effort: create a provenance explorer dashboard in Console for teams to inspect clusters and hit-rate of duplicate removal.

TODOs:
- [ ] Pitch lightweight schema to data-platform team (Priya)
- [ ] Add ephemeral snapshot hook to labeling UI (link to evidence_url generator)
- [ ] Implement simple fingerprint function in ingestion (hash of full text normalized + pipeline_tag)
- [ ] Run a 2-week experiment: enable dedupe in sampling and measure change in labeler throughput and model val metrics

Last quick thoughts:
- Provenance isn't just for deduping. It will help explain why certain errors recur (same upstream bug, same scrape pipeline) and speed up root cause analyses.
- Keep the first version small and automatable; expand fields later if we need them for audits and compliance.

Notes end.

(If returning to this: compare with "labeler-heuristic-drift-notes" and avoid duplicating heuristic lists. This doc focuses strictly on provenance + sampling consequences.)
